s.g: A spellcaster, conjurer, wizard, sorcerer or soothsayer who specializes in enchantments.
An instrument used to examine a bodily orifice or canal, or a hollow organ.
(historical) An ancient Greek philosopher, founder of the movement known as Epicureanism.
(clocks, mechanics) The linkage in a (watch) that gives impulses to the timekeeping element and periodically releases the gear train to move forward, advancing the clock's hands.
(transitive, figurative) To uncover; to bring to light.
having no fingers
A long, rectangular trunk or similar container that lies flat on the floor, especially one used for personal belongings and kept at the foot of a bed, commonly used in barracks and dormitories.
Sedimentary rock: a type of stone that is composed of small particles and easily shaped, most commonly sandstone or limestone.

Any of three species of large seabird in the genus Morus, of the family Sulidae. They have black and white bodies and long pointed wings, and hunt for fish by plunge diving and pursuing their prey underwater.
A poetic form mostly used for love poetry in Middle Eastern, South, and Central Asian poetry.
A hypothetical gauge boson that regulates the gravitational force. It would have a spin of 2 and zero rest mass.
Any of several waterbirds in the family Podicipedidae of the order Podicipediformes. They have strong, sharp bills, and lobate toes.
(tincture) In blazon, of the colour red.
(tincture) Red, e.g. on a coat of arms, typically represented in engraving by vertical parallel lines.
To lock away; to imprison, especially for breaking the law.
To confine; to shut up or enclose; to hem in.
The condition of being informal.
A hint; an obscure or indirect suggestion or notice; a remote or ambiguous reference.
(geometry) Having (at least) two sides of equal length, used especially of a triangle or trapezoid.
The phenomenon or level of unemployment in an economy.
A city, the administrative center of Krasnoyarsk Krai in Siberia, Russia.
A traditional article of clothing worn in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, consisting of a loose, collarless, long-sleeved, knee-length shirt worn by both men and women.
A type of hunting dog from Russia.
A cheerful or melodious accent when speaking.
Any of various ray-finned fishes of the tribe Pteroini (especially of the genus Pterois) in the family Scorpaenidae.
A Middle Eastern-style barbecue (cookout), or the barbecue (grill; cooking apparatus) it is cooked on.
An evergreen shrub or small tree, Pistacia lentiscus (mastic tree), native to the Mediterranean.
the tree's resin
A separate streamlined enclosure mounted on an aircraft to house, originally, an engine, and now also cargo or crew.
The capital city of Wallonia, Belgium.
Divination involving the dead or death.
(dentistry, periodontology) A serious form or stage of periodontal disease which may lead to loss of bone and falling out of teeth.
Any of various species of black, grey, or white seabirds in the order Procellariiformes.
The act by which something is pilfered; a petty theft.
(computing) Acronym of Portable Operating System Interface, a set of IEEE standards designed to provide application portability between UNIX variants.
The state of being a pundit.
Ancient Greek given name, particularly worn by the king of Epirus (319-272 BC) who defeated Romans in several battles, but sustained heavy losses, from which the term Pyrrhic victory was coined.
A cheesecloth bag of herbs or spices added during cooking and then removed before serving.
A currency unit of both ancient and modern Israel.
(astronomy) Relating to a measurement of time relative to the position of the stars.
Dirty, unwashed; disorderly.
Having an untidy appearance; unkempt.
One of the tiny pores in the epidermis of a leaf or stem through which gases and water vapor pass.
To get or be over without touching or resting on; to overcome.
A hypothetical particle that travels faster than the speed of light.
(enzyme, genetics) An enzyme in eukaryotic cells that adds a specific sequence of DNA to the telomeres of chromosomes after they divide; gives the chromosomes stability over time.
(psychoanalysis) The death drive in Freudian psychoanalysis.
One who believes in the existence of a god or gods.

A narrow pass on the east-central coast of Greece adjacent to the Maliakos Gulf, northwest of Athens. Its name is derived from its hot sulphur springs. It was the site of the Battle of Thermopylae, at which the Spartan King Leonidas stood off, for a time, the Persian armies of Xerxes.
Resembling a trailblazer; innovative or pioneering.
Describing any microorganism that has a single cell.
vigilance or the condition of being alert
A word used as a motto, as expressive of a principle, belief, or rule of action; a rallying cry.
(military, security) A prearranged reply to the challenge of a sentry or a guard; a password or signal by which friends can be known from enemies.
(uncountable, informal) Force on a pedal or increase to any fuel or power for an engine or motor.
A German- or Austrian-style sausage.
(botany) A vascular tissue in land plants primarily responsible for the distribution of water and minerals taken up by the roots; also the primary component of wood.
The vitality characteristic of youth.
A denial; a renunciation; denial of desire or self-interest. [First attested around 1350 to 1470.]

A calcium fluoride phosphate of variable composition, sometimes used in the manufacture of fertilizer, as a gemstone, and (in powdered form) as a pigment, and also produced biologically in bones and teeth.
(transitive) To divide and distribute portions of a whole.
(transitive) Specifically, to do so in a fair and equitable manner; to allocate proportionally.
To assert the truth of (something); to affirm (something) with confidence; to declare (something) in a positive manner.
To justify or prove (an allegation or plea that one has made).
The bristle or beard of barley, oats, grasses, etc., or any similar bristlelike appendage; arista.
